# Nicholas Howell and Full Stack Technologies

> Nicholas Howell is a CTO, founding engineer, and full-stack developer based in
> Saint Petersburg, Florida. Full Stack Technologies, LLC is the studio he leads.

## Brand boundaries

The personal site explains what working one-on-one with Nicholas is like: hands-on
building, candid conversation, guidance, and the experience behind his decisions.
Full Stack Technologies helps founders take apps and AI prototypes into production, and owns
the practical blog, AI playbook, and prompt library. Nicholas authors the FST articles.
The personal site links to selected FST resources rather than hosting those libraries.
Valid former personal resource URLs permanently redirect to FST; unknown paths remain 404s.
Use each page's canonical URL when citing it.

## Personal pages (relative to the personal site's origin)

- /: Meet Nick, what working together feels like, experience, and selected work.
- /home/how-i-work: Direct collaboration, progress, decisions, and handoff with Nicholas.
- /home/working-through-a-build: A Timetrack example of explaining decisions and checking behavior together.
- /home/straight-answers: Questions about fit and working with Nicholas.
- /home/off-clock: Family, travel, and ice hockey.

## Practical blog (Full Stack Technologies only)

- https://fullstacktechnologiesllc.com/blog: Product engineering guides by Nicholas Howell.
- https://fullstacktechnologiesllc.com/blog/timetrack-session-reporting: Preserve short manual entries, explain parallel sessions, and make report calculations inspectable.
- https://fullstacktechnologiesllc.com/blog/scope-first-software-release: Scope a complete user journey.
- https://fullstacktechnologiesllc.com/blog/review-ai-generated-code: Review behavior, access, writes, tests, and recovery.
- https://fullstacktechnologiesllc.com/blog/repair-or-rewrite: Compare repairs, component replacement, and rewrite.
- https://fullstacktechnologiesllc.com/blog/ai-prototype-to-production: Check access, data, integrations, deployment, and recovery before launch.
- https://fullstacktechnologiesllc.com/blog/build-vs-buy-software: Compare building, buying, and integrating with an illustrative total-cost example.

## Product examples (both sites, with distinct framing)

The personal pages explain Nicholas's contribution and design/engineering decisions.
The studio pages explain the user problems and capabilities relevant to a product engagement.
The interfaces are shared; their presence is not a claim of adoption or client outcomes.

- /paradox/overview: Interactive storytelling, branching timelines, onboarding, and search.
- /timetrack/overview: AI session activity, parallel time, audit records, and reports.
  Session time differs from elapsed human time; billing depends on the client agreement.
  Selected metadata flows from local hooks to user-controlled hosted services. Optional
  model features have separate data flows; self-hosted does not mean entirely on-device.
- /constellation/overview: Multi-client priorities, plan branches, forecast ranges, and client status.
- /helm/overview: One decision at a time across clients and AI agents, with a decision deck, client boards, plain-language rules, and scoped access.
- /nemo/overview: Portable AI memory: imported ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and Grok history distilled into identities, assembled into compact context for any model, encrypted on device.
- /snakenfriends/overview: Mobile snake game: a 60-sector campaign, ranked 1v1 arena series, and a deterministic engine whose runs are replayed on the server before a score counts.
- /coverly/overview: Insurance policy wallet: declarations pages read into fields you confirm, plain-English summaries, answers that quote the policy page they came from, and renewal reminders.

## AI playbook (Full Stack Technologies only)

- https://fullstacktechnologiesllc.com/ai: Workflow, people, and tool choices.
- https://fullstacktechnologiesllc.com/ai/workflow: AI across discovery, design, build, review, release, and maintenance.
- https://fullstacktechnologiesllc.com/ai/models: Dated tool and model examples with official sources.
- https://fullstacktechnologiesllc.com/ai/why-an-engineer: Architecture, data boundaries, verification, and ownership.
- https://fullstacktechnologiesllc.com/ai/why-a-designer: Usability, design systems, accessibility, and handoff.
- https://fullstacktechnologiesllc.com/ai/lean-team: Smaller delivery teams versus in-house capacity.
- https://fullstacktechnologiesllc.com/ai/offshore-tradeoffs: Delivery setup, direct access, overlap, and ownership.
- https://fullstacktechnologiesllc.com/ai/resources: Tools and project-level usage and billing questions.
- https://fullstacktechnologiesllc.com/ai/community-research: Linked Reddit accounts, distinct from benchmarks.

Nicholas uses Claude /design for product design, Claude Code generally for implementation,
and Codex for reviews, images and logo exploration, landing pages, and websites. Some tasks
use both. Model examples are dated guidance, not a claim about every project's settings.
There is no universal savings figure or AI billing policy asserted here.

## Prompt library (Full Stack Technologies only)

- https://fullstacktechnologiesllc.com/prompts: Timing, inputs, and checks for each template.
- https://fullstacktechnologiesllc.com/prompts/discovery: Brief and acceptance criteria.
- https://fullstacktechnologiesllc.com/prompts/design: Product design and visual/page briefs.
- https://fullstacktechnologiesllc.com/prompts/implementation: Bounded changes and tool-to-tool handoff.
- https://fullstacktechnologiesllc.com/prompts/review-release: Evidence-based review and release readiness.

Templates are starting points. People own design acceptance, engineering verification,
access decisions, and release authorization.

Use the current site's message drawer or email admin@fullstacktechnologiesllc.com. Include the users,
problem, current system, and constraints. Commercial studio services are described on FST.
